raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Every op registered with `register_custom_op` is called through `torch.ops.sglang.<name>`, even in plain eager execution. The op is registered for a single device key and has no autograd formula. So for ordinary tensors the dispatcher does nothing except box the arguments and re-enter the same Python implementation, and that costs several microseconds per call. For diffusion models this is a noticeable share of host time per denoising step. In a py-spy profile of FLUX.2, Qwen-Image and Ideogram (H200, 2 GPUs, eager, at a size where the host bounds the step), `torch/_ops.py __call__` alone accounts for 5–8% of host time. On Grace hosts (GB200/GB300) and with several TP ranks, the step is host-bound and this time reaches end-to-end latency.

## Modifications

`CustomOpWrapper.real_impl` (`sglang/srt/utils/custom_op.py`) now returns a thin caller. It calls the op's Python function directly only for plain device tensors under `no_grad` / `inference_mode`, which is how both srt and multimodal_gen run. It calls the registered op in every other case:
- under `torch.compile` / export tracing (`torch.compiler.is_compiling()`);
- while a dispatch mode is active: fake tensors, `make_fx`, `FlopCounterMode`, or any `TorchDispatchMode`;
- while a `TorchFunctionMode` is active;
- while the profiler is enabled, so traces keep their `sglang::<op>` spans;
- with grad enabled;
- when an argument is a tensor subclass, or a host or meta tensor. These keep their previous `NotImplementedError` or fake output.
- when another function registered the name first;
- when kernel API logging is enabled.

The dispatcher sets no device guard for Python-registered kernels, so the current-device behavior is unchanged. One difference remains: the dispatcher converted arguments to the schema's types (e.g. a 0-d tensor passed for a `float`), and the direct call passes them as given. The call sites checked pass Python scalars.

No memory is involved. Compiled graphs are unchanged, because they reference `torch.ops.sglang.*` directly. Ops registered with `direct_register_custom_op` and called as `torch.ops.sglang.*` are untouched.

## Accuracy Tests

The same Python implementation runs with the same arguments, so outputs are identical. In every end-to-end configuration below, the output image md5 matched main.

`test/registered/unit/utils/test_custom_op_eager_direct.py` checks four things:
- an eager call enters the implementation directly;
- a `TorchDispatchMode` still sees `sglang.<op>`;
- grad mode, a `TorchFunctionMode` or a tensor subclass goes through the dispatcher;
- the profiler records the op;
- host tensors are still rejected;
- a name registered first by another function keeps that function;
- `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` traces the op.

On GB300 (sm103) and H200, the existing suites that exercise these ops pass:
- diffusion kernels: `test_modulate`, `test_activation`, `test_rope`, `test_complex_rope`, `test_qknorm_rope_out_of_place`, `test_flux2_gated_resnorm`, `test_model_fast_paths`, `test_sites`, `test_residual_gate_fp32`;
- compile and communication: `test_regional_torch_compile`, `test_group_coordinator_compiled_all_reduce`, `test_torch_compile_decoration`.

The only exception is `test_rope`, whose three `test_anima_rope_bit_exact` failures also occur on main on that GPU.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Base `8afe107`, torch 2.13, triton 3.7.1, GB300 (Grace host). Processes were pinned to the GPUs' NUMA node.

**Host time per call** (µs, inference mode):

| op | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `residual_gate_add` | 30.8 | 25.9 |
| `modulate_scale_shift` | 19.0 | 13.8 |
| `fused_silu_mul_bitexact` | 28.0 | 23.9 |
| `fused_rope_rotate_half_bitexact` | 31.5 | 25.4 |
| `qknorm_complex_rope_cuda` | 27.1 | 18.7 |
| `fused_inplace_qknorm_rope` | 15.3 | 8.8 |

On an x86 host (H200, Xeon 8558P) the dispatcher is cheaper and the saving is 0.2–2.4 µs per call.

**End to end.** Client wall clock, median, TP2 eager on GB300 ×2. Servers for main and this PR were resident together and requests alternated over 10 pairs.

| | main | this PR | | this PR faster in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2.1 512² | 1568.3 ms | 1495.9 ms | −4.6% | 10/10 |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 1024² | 1686.5 ms | 1583.3 ms | −6.1% | 10/10 |
| FLUX.1-dev 512² | 3848.7 ms | 3798.2 ms | −1.3% | 10/10 |
| FLUX.1-dev 1024² | 4029.3 ms | 3841.6 ms | −4.7% | 10/10 |

**Stacking with #43859.** #43859 replays small Triton wrappers' launches; it is independent of this PR and the gains add up. The table below was measured with an earlier revision of this PR, before the profiler, grad and device guards were added. Its per-call saving was the same as the final version's. All four servers were resident together, with requests rotated over 8 rounds.

| | main | this PR | #43859 | both |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2.1 512² | 1536.9 ms | 1452.8 ms | 1424.3 ms | 1323.0 ms (−13.9%) |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 1024² | 1632.3 ms | 1561.6 ms | 1520.6 ms | 1437.0 ms (−12.0%) |
| FLUX.1-dev 512² | 3930.4 ms | 3745.6 ms | 3701.6 ms | 3539.8 ms (−9.9%) |
| FLUX.1-dev 1024² | 3966.7 ms | 3809.9 ms | 3763.9 ms | 3650.1 ms (−8.0%) |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

 from __future__ import annotations
 
+import functools
 import inspect

+from sglang.kernels.kernel_api_logging import _KERNEL_API_LOG_LEVEL, debug_torch_op
 
 F = TypeVar("F", bound=Callable)
 
@@ -130,6 +131,45 @@ def decorator(op_func: Callable) -> Callable:
     return decorator
 
 
+_PLAIN_TENSORS = (torch.Tensor, torch.nn.Parameter)
+# Bound once: these run on every eager call of every op.
+_is_compiling = torch.compiler.is_compiling
+_dispatch_modes = torch._C._len_torch_dispatch_stack
+_function_modes = torch._C._is_torch_function_mode_enabled
+_profiling = torch._C._autograd._profiler_enabled
+_grad_enabled = torch.is_grad_enabled
+
+
+def _call_directly_in_eager(op_func: Callable, op: Callable) -> Callable:
+    """Call ``op_func`` itself in plain eager execution, skipping the dispatcher.
+
+    The op is registered for one device key with no autograd formula, so for plain
+    CUDA tensors under no_grad the dispatcher only re-enters ``op_func``, at several
+    microseconds a call. Everything else keeps the registered op: tracing, dispatch
+    and function modes, the profiler (which records the op), autograd, tensor
+    subclasses, and tensors on other devices (which the op rejects or fakes).
+    """
+
+    @functools.wraps(op_func)
+    def call(*args, **kwargs):
+        if (
+            _is_compiling()
+            or _dispatch_modes()
+            or _function_modes()
+            or _profiling()
+            or _grad_enabled()
+        ):
+            return op(*args, **kwargs)
+        for a in (*args, *kwargs.values()):
+            if isinstance(a, torch.Tensor) and (
+                type(a) not in _PLAIN_TENSORS or not a.is_cuda
+            ):
+                return op(*args, **kwargs)
+        return op_func(*args, **kwargs)
+
+    return call
+

@@ -0,0 +1,134 @@
+"""``register_custom_op`` ops skip the dispatcher in plain eager execution.
+
+Only plain device tensors under no_grad take the direct call. Tracing, dispatch and
+function modes, the profiler, autograd, tensor subclasses, host tensors and a name
+registered by another function first all keep the registered op.
+"""
+
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+from torch.overrides import TorchFunctionMode
+from torch.utils._python_dispatch import TorchDispatchMode
+
+from sglang.srt.utils.custom_op import register_custom_op
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=15, stage="base-b", runner_config="1-gpu-small")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="CUDA required")
+
+calls = []  # (function, its caller's frame name)
+
+
+def _fake_add(x, y):
+    return torch.empty_like(x)
+
+
+@register_custom_op(
+    op_name="test_eager_direct_add", mutates_args=[], fake_impl=_fake_add
+)
+def eager_direct_add(x: torch.Tensor, y: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    calls.append(("eager_direct_add", sys._getframe(1).f_code.co_name))
+    return x + y
+
+
+def _operands(device="cuda"):
+    return torch.randn(8, device=device), torch.randn(8, device=device)
+
+
+def _took_direct_call():
+    return calls[-1] == ("eager_direct_add", "call")
+
+
+@torch.no_grad()
+def test_eager_call_skips_the_dispatcher():
+    x, y = _operands()
+    assert torch.equal(eager_direct_add(x, y), x + y)
+    assert _took_direct_call()
+
+
+class _SeenOps(TorchDispatchMode):
+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.ops = []
+
+    def __torch_dispatch__(self, func, types, args=(), kwargs=None):
+        self.ops.append(str(func))
+        return func(*args, **(kwargs or {}))
+
+
+@torch.no_grad()
+def test_dispatch_mode_sees_the_registered_op():
+    x, y = _operands()
+    with _SeenOps() as mode:
+        assert torch.equal(eager_direct_add(x, y), x + y)
+    assert "sglang.test_eager_direct_add.default" in mode.ops
+
+
+class _Passthrough(TorchFunctionMode):
+    def __torch_function__(self, func, types, args=(), kwargs=None):
+        return func(*args, **(kwargs or {}))
+
+
+class _Sub(torch.Tensor):
+    pass
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("case", ["grad", "function_mode", "subclass"])
+def test_other_contexts_use_the_dispatcher(case):
+    x, y = _operands()
+    if case == "grad":
+        out = eager_direct_add(x, y)
+    else:
+        with torch.no_grad():
+            if case == "subclass":
+                out = eager_direct_add(x.as_subclass(_Sub), y)
+            else:
+                with _Passthrough():
+                    out = eager_direct_add(x, y)
+    assert torch.equal(out, x + y)
+    assert not _took_direct_call()
+
+
+@torch.no_grad()
+def test_profiler_records_the_op():
+    x, y = _operands()
+    with torch.profiler.profile(
+        activities=[torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CPU]
+    ) as prof:
+        eager_direct_add(x, y)
+    assert any("test_eager_direct_add" in event.name for event in prof.events())
+
+
+@torch.no_grad()
+def test_host_tensors_are_still_rejected():
+    with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError):
+        eager_direct_add(*_operands("cpu"))
+
+
+@torch.no_grad()
+def test_a_name_registered_first_elsewhere_keeps_that_function():
+    def other(x: torch.Tensor, y: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        calls.append(("other", sys._getframe(1).f_code.co_name))
+        return x - y
+
+    second = register_custom_op(
+        op_name="test_eager_direct_add", mutates_args=[], fake_impl=_fake_add
+    )(other)
+    x, y = _operands()
+    assert torch.equal(second(x, y), x + y)
+    assert calls[-1][0] == "eager_direct_add"
+
+
+def test_compile_traces_the_registered_op():
+    x, y = _operands()
+    compiled = torch.compile(
+        lambda a, b: eager_direct_add(a, b) * 2, fullgraph=True, backend="eager"
+    )
+    assert torch.equal(compiled(x, y), (x + y) * 2)
